concept.definition: A bottleneck building block is a residual function composed of three stacked convolutional layers (1×1, 3×3, 1×1) that reduces and then restores the number of feature map channels, so that the computationally expensive 3×3 convolution operates on a compact intermediate representation.
concept.simpleExplanation: Instead of using two 3×3 convolutions directly, the bottleneck block first uses a 1×1 convolution to shrink the number of channels (compressing the data), then applies a 3×3 convolution on this smaller representation, and finally uses another 1×1 convolution to expand the channels back. This design makes the network much deeper without significantly increasing computational cost.
concept.analogy: Imagine you need to move many heavy boxes across a room. Instead of carrying each box directly one at a time (costly), you first consolidate items into fewer, larger carts (1×1 reduction), move the carts efficiently (3×3), then unpack them back into many boxes on the other side (1×1 expansion). The heavy lifting happens only on a compact load.
concept.whyUsedHere: The authors use the bottleneck block for very deep ResNets (50, 101, 152 layers) on ImageNet to keep computational cost low while increasing depth dramatically. They note that identity shortcuts become even more important here because adding a projection shortcut would double both parameters and time complexity since the shortcut connects two high-dimensional ends of the block.
prerequisites: Convolutional layer and feature map channels
Residual learning (the core idea of F(x)+x)
FLOPs (floating-point operations) as a measure of complexity
